stalled-download.steps: Loads the photo from the slow server, which sends half of it and then holds the rest. Passes on onError, about 15 seconds later (onLoad fails it); the server is then released.
stalled-download.shows: Blank space (64 points, no background): the image never loads.

description.checks: Images with one cacheKey and different urls when one url fails: on Android, which shares one download per cacheKey, the download is retried with another of the cacheKey's urls.
description.steps: In each case the first image's url 404s; the slow server holds that response until another image with the same cacheKey has mounted. The images have no background, so where nothing shows the screen is white.

shared-download-retry.checks: An image whose url works loads when another url with the same cacheKey 404s, and the image of that url gets onError (on Android, which shares downloads by cacheKey, the second image's request joins the first's download and is retried with its own url once that fails).
shared-download-retry.steps: A small image loads a missing url from the slow server with a cacheKey; once the server has the request it holds the 404, a large image of the photo with the same cacheKey mounts, and a second later the 404 is sent. Passes when the small one has had onError and the large one has loaded.
shared-download-retry.shows: Blank space where the 404 is (32 points), then a large (64-point) photo of a pug in a blanket.

retry-progress.checks: After a cacheKey's first url fails, its other urls load from one download, and each image gets its own progress (Android downloaded both urls once the first had failed, and sent both downloads' progress to both images, so the slow one got 1 from the fast one's download while its own still came).
retry-progress.steps: A small image loads a missing url from the slow server with a cacheKey (the 404 held); then a medium image of a fast url and a large image of a slow one mount with the same cacheKey, and a second later the 404 is sent. Passes when the small one has had onError, the other two have loaded, each got onProgress 1 at most a second before its onLoad, and the server got 2 requests on Android (one download for both) or 3 on iOS (which shares downloads by url).
retry-progress.shows: Blank space where the 404 is (32 points), then a medium (48-point) and a large (64-point) photo of a pug in a blanket.

retry-latest-url.checks: After a cacheKey's url fails, the retry downloads the latest of its other urls, since they're the same image (Android tried the other urls one at a time, the earliest first).
retry-latest-url.steps: A small image loads a missing url from the slow server with a cacheKey (the 404 held); then a medium image of another url mounts with that cacheKey, and half a second later a large image of a third url. A second later the 404 is sent. Passes when the small one has had onError, the other two have loaded, and, on Android, the server got the latest url's request and none for the earlier one's (iOS shares downloads by url, so it downloads both).
retry-latest-url.shows: Blank space where the 404 is (32 points), then a medium (48-point) and a large (64-point) photo of a pug in a blanket.

retry-newer-url.checks: A newer url that joins a cacheKey's retry is downloaded when the retry fails too (Android retried a failed download once, so the newer url was never requested).
retry-newer-url.steps: A small image loads a missing url from the slow server with a cacheKey (the 404 held); a medium image of a second missing url mounts with that cacheKey, and the first 404 is sent, so the retry downloads the second url (also held). While it's held, a large image of a url that works mounts with the cacheKey, then the second 404 is sent. Passes when the first two have had onError and the large one has loaded.
retry-newer-url.shows: Blank space twice (32 and 48 points, the two urls that 404), then a large (64-point) photo of a pug in a blanket, which isn't compared: it can come from either of two decodes.

description.checks: FastImage.clearDiskCache also clears the HTTP cache that cache: 'web' images use.

web-cache-clear.checks: FastImage.clearDiskCache also clears the HTTP cache of cache: 'web' images, so the image is downloaded again (clearDiskCache left that cache, Android's and on iOS the app's shared NSURLCache, so the image came from there).
web-cache-clear.steps: Loads a photo with cache: 'web' from a url the server marks as cacheable for an hour, then calls FastImage.clearMemoryCache and FastImage.clearDiskCache and loads it again in a new view. Passes when both clears resolved ok and the server got two requests for it.
web-cache-clear.shows: A photo of a pug in a blanket (the second load). An empty gray square means the second load never finished.

description.checks: A cache: 'web' image preloaded right after FastImage.clearDiskCache resolves is downloaded again, not taken from the HTTP cache.

web-cache-clear-preload.checks: A cache: 'web' image preloaded right after FastImage.clearDiskCache resolves is downloaded again (on iOS, the HTTP cache's removal took effect a few milliseconds after clearDiskCache resolved, and a load in that time got the old response).
web-cache-clear-preload.steps: Ten times, with a new url each time that the server marks as cacheable for an hour: preloads the photo with cache: 'web', clears the memory and disk caches, preloads it again as soon as the clears resolve, and asks the server how many times it was requested. Passes when every preload and clear succeeded and each url was requested twice.
web-cache-clear-preload.shows: An empty gray square: the case only preloads.

description.checks: FastImage.preload: what it downloads and caches, the headers it sends, how many sources it loads at once, its results, and the source values it accepts.

preload.checks: FastImage.preload, then a view of the same image, which loads.
preload.steps: Preloads a photo, and half a second later shows it in a view. Passes on the view's onLoad.
preload.shows: A photo of a pug in a blanket.

preload-headers.checks: Headers given to FastImage.preload aren't sent with other images (#571: iOS set them on the shared downloader, so every later request sent them).
preload-headers.steps: Preloads an image with the header x-token, then half a second later shows another image from a url the server answers with a 400 if the request has an x-token header. Passes on onLoad; onError fails it.
preload-headers.shows: A green aurora over a tree. An empty gray square means the image's request had the preload's header (the server answers it with a 400).

preload-reuse.checks: An image shown once FastImage.preload has resolved comes from the preload, not a new download (#657: on Android, a view shown while the preload was still in flight downloaded it again; awaiting the result avoids that).
preload-reuse.steps: Preloads the photo from a url new each launch, and shows it in a view once the preload resolves ok. Passes when the view has loaded and the server got one request for it.
preload-reuse.shows: A photo of a pug in a blanket.

preload-results.checks: FastImage.preload resolves with each source's result, in order: ok with its size for the ones that loaded, not ok with an error for the others.
preload-results.steps: Preloads six sources: a 200×200 photo, a url that 404s, an empty uri, null, a 120×120 photo the server only sends with the header x-token (given), and another that needs the header (not given). Passes when the results are 200x200, failed, failed, failed, 120x120, failed, and every failed one has an error.
preload-results.shows: An empty gray square: the case only preloads.

preload-limit.checks: FastImage.preload loads a few sources at a time (3, or SDWebImagePrefetcher's limit on iOS), so a long list doesn't hold up the images the app shows.
preload-limit.steps: Preloads four images from the slow server (about a second each), then asks the server how many it was sending at the same time. Passes when all four loaded, from four requests, with at most 3 at once (without the limit, both platforms load all 4 at once).
preload-limit.shows: An empty gray square: the case only preloads.

preload-disk.checks: FastImage.preload with memoryCache: false (to disk only, without decoding) still reports the image's size, and a view then loads it from the disk cache.
preload-disk.steps: Preloads a 200×200 photo with memoryCache: false, then shows it in a view with the same source. Passes when the preload resolved ok with 200×200, the view has loaded, and the server got one request.
preload-disk.shows: A photo of a pug in a blanket.

preload-cache-only.checks: FastImage.preload with cache: 'cacheOnly' of an image that isn't cached fails without a request, as a view does (#406: iOS downloaded it, since preload didn't follow cache).
preload-cache-only.steps: Preloads the logo from a url new each launch with cache: 'cacheOnly'. Passes when the result is not ok and the server got no request for it.
preload-cache-only.shows: An empty gray square: the case only preloads.

preload-retry.checks: A url whose first response was an HTML page (status 200) is downloaded again by the next preload (#394: iOS failed it without a request until the app was relaunched, since views retried failed urls but preloads didn't; Android kept the page in Glide's disk cache; iOS could also give a preload right after the failure the failed download's error, without a request, while SDWebImage was still finishing it).
preload-retry.steps: For 40 urls, each new, that the server first answers with a captive portal's HTML page and then with the photo: preloads it (it fails), preloads it again, and checks the second succeeded from a second request. Then shows the first url in a view; passes on its onLoad.
preload-retry.shows: A photo of a pug in a blanket. An empty gray square means a preload failed before the view was shown.

preload-unknown-values.checks: FastImage.preload loads sources with a cache or priority value Fast Image doesn't know, with the default (Android threw for them).
preload-unknown-values.steps: Preloads the photo three times (three urls) with cache: 'reload', priority: 'urgent', and cache: 1 with priority: true. Passes when all three resolve ok with 200x200.
preload-unknown-values.shows: An empty gray square: the case only preloads.

description.checks: Urls whose response isn't the image (an HTML page, a 503, a 404): a later load downloads them again, and a failure isn't requested twice; and an image sent with the wrong Content-Type still loads.

preload-retry-web.checks: A cache: 'web' url whose first response was an HTML page (status 200) is downloaded again by the next preload (both platforms kept the page in the HTTP cache of web images, so later loads failed; iOS could still get it from there right after the failure, about once in tens of urls, so it tries many).
preload-retry-web.steps: For 40 urls, each new, that the server first answers with a captive portal's HTML page (cacheable for an hour) and then with the photo: preloads it with cache: 'web' (it fails), preloads it again, and checks the second succeeded from a second request. Then shows the first url in a view; passes on its onLoad.
preload-retry-web.shows: A photo of a pug in a blanket. An empty gray square means a preload failed before the view was shown.

view-retry.checks: A url whose first response was an HTML page (status 200) loads in the next view (Android kept the page in Glide's disk cache, so the second view failed too).
view-retry.steps: Shows a url the server first answers with a captive portal's HTML page, then with the photo: the view gets onError, and a new view of the same url mounts. Passes when the new view has loaded and the server got two requests.
view-retry.shows: A photo of a pug in a blanket (the second view).

reload.checks: The ref's reload(): it downloads a url that failed again, and loads an image that has loaded again from the cache, with its events each time.
reload.steps: Shows a url whose first request fails with a 503; on onError, calls reload(), which downloads it and shows it; once it has loaded, calls reload() again. Passes when the server got two requests and the events were onLoadStart, onError, onLoadStart, onLoad, onLoadStart, onLoad.
reload.shows: A photo of a pug in a blanket.

mislabeled.checks: An image the server sends with Content-Type: text/plain still loads (Android fails a response that isn't an image only if its bytes aren't an image either).
mislabeled.steps: Loads the photo, sent as text/plain. Passes on onLoad; onError fails it.
mislabeled.shows: A photo of a pug in a blanket.

web-404.checks: A cache: 'web' url that 404s fails with one request (Android loaded it again with the client without the HTTP cache: two requests).
web-404.steps: Preloads a missing image with cache: 'web'. Passes when the result is not ok and the server got one request for it.
web-404.shows: An empty gray square: the case only preloads.

description.checks: source.cacheKey, which caches an image under a key of its own instead of its url, and memoryCache: false.

cache-key.checks: source.cacheKey: an image whose url has another token but the same cacheKey comes from the cache (#524: a key for images whose url changes, like short-lived private urls).
cache-key.steps: Loads a photo with ?token=a and a cacheKey; once it has loaded, a second view (downsample false) loads it with ?token=b and the same cacheKey. Passes when the second has loaded and the server got no request for the token=b url.
cache-key.shows: Two photos of a pug in a blanket side by side. An empty gray square on the right means the second never loaded.

cache-key-preload.checks: source.cacheKey with FastImage.preload: a preloaded image is found under its cacheKey by a view of another url.
cache-key-preload.steps: Preloads a photo with ?token=a and a cacheKey; once the preload resolves, a view loads it with ?token=b and the same cacheKey. Passes when the view has loaded and the server got no request for the token=b url.
cache-key-preload.shows: An empty gray square (the preload has no view), then a photo of a pug in a blanket.

cache-key-downsample.checks: source.cacheKey with downsample: a view that downsamples finds the file downloaded for the cacheKey instead of requesting its own url.
cache-key-downsample.steps: Loads a photo with ?token=a and a cacheKey; once it has loaded, a second view with downsample loads it with ?token=b and the same cacheKey. Passes when the second has loaded and the server got no request for the token=b url.
cache-key-downsample.shows: Two photos of a pug in a blanket side by side.

memory-cache-off.checks: memoryCache: false: the image shows, and a second view of it loads from the disk cache.
memory-cache-off.steps: Loads a photo with memoryCache: false; once it has loaded, a second view with the same source mounts. Passes when the second has loaded and the server got one request (that it isn't kept in memory isn't visible here).
memory-cache-off.shows: Two photos of a pug in a blanket side by side. An empty gray square on the right means the second never loaded.

description.checks: Views with cache: 'cacheOnly', or React Native's 'only-if-cached', for an image that isn't cached.

cache-only-miss.checks: A view with cache: 'cacheOnly' for an image that isn't cached gets onError and onLoadEnd (not ok), without a request (#1315: iOS sent onLoad and onLoadEnd for an image it didn't have).
cache-only-miss.steps: Loads a photo of a pug that nothing has loaded (a url only this case uses) with cache: 'cacheOnly'. When onError fires, asks the image server how many requests it got for the url. Passes if it got none, onLoadEnd's ok was false, and onLoad never fired.
cache-only-miss.shows: An empty gray square: the image is never loaded. The pug here would mean it was downloaded.

only-if-cached-miss.checks: React Native's cache: 'only-if-cached' works as cacheOnly: an image that isn't cached gets onError and onLoadEnd (not ok), without a request.
only-if-cached-miss.steps: Loads a photo of a pug that nothing has loaded (a url only this case uses) with cache: 'only-if-cached'. When onError fires, asks the image server how many requests it got for the url. Passes if it got none, onLoadEnd's ok was false, and onLoad never fired.
only-if-cached-miss.shows: An empty gray square: the image is never loaded. The pug here would mean it was downloaded.

description.checks: source.diskCache false: the image isn't kept on disk or in an HTTP cache, or read from them.

disk-cache-off.checks: diskCache: false keeps an image off disk: a second view of the same size gets it from memory, a larger one downloads it again, and getCachePath doesn't find it.
disk-cache-off.steps: Loads a 200×200 photo of a pug in a 48×48 view with diskCache: false. On its onLoad, adds a second 48×48 view and an 88×88 one with the same source. When the large one loads, passes if the image server got two requests (the first view's and the large one's), and getCachePath resolves not ok for the uri with cache: 'cacheOnly' and for the source itself.
disk-cache-off.shows: The pug photo three times: two small, then a larger one.

disk-cache-off-web.checks: diskCache: false with cache: 'web': each view downloads the image, though the server lets caches keep it and a preload stored its url on disk.
disk-cache-off-web.steps: Preloads the pug photo's url (the default cache), from a route the image server sends with Cache-Control: max-age=3600. Then a view loads it with cache: 'web' and diskCache: false, and on its onLoad a second view of the same size does too. Passes when the second loads, if the image server got three requests (the preload's and each view's).
disk-cache-off-web.shows: The pug photo twice, side by side.

description.checks: FastImage.getCachePath: the file of a source's image in the disk cache, or not ok when there isn't one.

cache-path.checks: getCachePath for an image a view has loaded gives its file in the disk cache.
cache-path.steps: A view loads a 120×120 photo of a green aurora over a tree. On its onLoad, calls getCachePath with the same source and shows the file it gives in a second view, as a file:// uri. Passes once that view loads and the image server got one request for the url (the first view's).
cache-path.shows: The aurora photo twice: the view, then its file.

cache-path-key.checks: getCachePath for an image with a cacheKey, which a view has loaded, gives its file.
cache-path-key.steps: A view loads the aurora photo with a cacheKey. On its onLoad, calls getCachePath with the same uri and cacheKey and shows the file it gives in a second view. Passes once that view loads and the image server got one request.
cache-path-key.shows: The aurora photo twice: the view, then its file.

cache-path-download.checks: getCachePath for an image that wasn't loaded downloads it and gives its file.
cache-path-download.steps: Calls getCachePath for the aurora photo (a url nothing has loaded) on mount, and shows the file it gives. Passes once that view loads and the image server got exactly one request (the download).
cache-path-download.shows: An empty gray square (no view loads the url), then the aurora photo from the file.

cache-path-cache-only.checks: getCachePath with cache: 'cacheOnly' for an image that wasn't loaded resolves not ok, without downloading it.
cache-path-cache-only.steps: Calls getCachePath for the aurora photo (a url nothing has loaded) with cache: 'cacheOnly' on mount. Passes if it resolves not ok and the image server got no request for the url.
cache-path-cache-only.shows: Two empty gray squares: no view loads the url, and there is no file to show. The photo on the right would mean it was downloaded.

cache-path-404.checks: getCachePath for a url that 404s resolves not ok, with the status in its error.
cache-path-404.steps: Calls getCachePath on mount for a url the image server answers with a 404. Passes if it resolves not ok with an error that has 404 in it.
cache-path-404.shows: Two empty gray squares: there's no image and no file.

cache-path-space.checks: getCachePath for a url with a space in it gives its file (iOS caches such a url escaped).
cache-path-space.steps: A view loads the aurora photo from a url with a space in its query (name=a b). On its onLoad, calls getCachePath with the same source and shows the file it gives. Passes once that view loads and the image server got one request.
cache-path-space.shows: The aurora photo twice: the view, then its file.

description.checks: More getCachePath cases: cache: 'web' images, only a cacheKey, and an image still downloading.

cache-path-web.checks: getCachePath for an image loaded with cache: 'web' gives its file (on Android, in the HTTP cache).
cache-path-web.steps: A view loads the aurora photo with cache: 'web', from a url the image server sends with Cache-Control: max-age=3600. On its onLoad, calls getCachePath with the same source and shows the file it gives. Passes once that view loads and the image server got one request.
cache-path-web.shows: The aurora photo twice: the view, then its file.

cache-path-web-cache-only.checks: getCachePath with cache: 'cacheOnly' finds an image a view loaded with cache: 'web', on both platforms.
cache-path-web-cache-only.steps: A view loads the aurora photo with cache: 'web' (sent with max-age=3600). On its onLoad, calls getCachePath with the same uri and cache: 'cacheOnly' and shows the file it gives. Passes once that view loads and the image server got one request.
cache-path-web-cache-only.shows: The aurora photo twice: the view, then its file.

cache-path-key-only.checks: getCachePath with only a cacheKey (no uri) finds the file of an image a view loaded with that cacheKey.
cache-path-key-only.steps: A view loads the aurora photo with a cacheKey. On its onLoad, calls getCachePath with only the cacheKey and shows the file it gives. Passes once that view loads and the image server got one request (the view's).
cache-path-key-only.shows: The aurora photo twice: the view, then its file.

cache-path-key-only-missing.checks: getCachePath with only a cacheKey that isn't cached resolves not ok, without a request.
cache-path-key-only-missing.steps: Calls getCachePath on mount with only a cacheKey nothing has used. Passes if it resolves not ok and the image server got no request.
cache-path-key-only-missing.shows: Two empty gray squares: no view loads the image, and there's no file to show.

cache-path-while-loading.checks: getCachePath while a view is still downloading the image gives its file, and shares the view's download (Android downloaded it a second time with Glide).
cache-path-while-loading.steps: A view loads the aurora photo from the slow server (in 8 parts, 150 ms apart). On its onLoadStart, calls getCachePath with the same source and shows the file it gives. Passes once that view loads and the slow server got one request for both.
cache-path-while-loading.shows: The aurora photo twice: the view, then its file.

cache-path-data-uri.checks: getCachePath for a data uri stores its image in the disk cache and gives its file (Android resolved not ok: "Not a remote image").
cache-path-data-uri.steps: Calls getCachePath on mount for an 8×8 yellow PNG data uri that no view has shown (it has a parameter of its own), and shows the file it gives. Passes once that view loads.
cache-path-data-uri.shows: An empty gray square, then a yellow square from the file.

description.checks: getCachePath after FastImage.clearDiskCache(), for an image getCachePath downloaded.

cache-path-after-clear.checks: After clearDiskCache, getCachePath with cache: 'cacheOnly' doesn't find an image, and without it downloads the image again (#1294: Android kept the file's path in Glide's memory cache, so both gave the old path, though the clear had deleted the file).
cache-path-after-clear.steps: getCachePath downloads the aurora photo; then awaits FastImage.clearDiskCache(); then getCachePath with cache: 'cacheOnly', and then without it. Passes if the cacheOnly call resolves not ok, the other gives a file that's there, and the image server got two requests (the first download and the one after the clear).
cache-path-after-clear.shows: An empty gray square: the case shows no image.

description.checks: getCachePath after FastImage.clearDiskCache(), for an image a view showed.

cache-path-after-clear-loaded.checks: After clearDiskCache, getCachePath with cache: 'cacheOnly' doesn't find an image a view showed, and without it downloads the image again (#1294: Android kept the result of its lookup on disk in Glide's memory cache, so both gave the old path, though the clear had deleted the file).
cache-path-after-clear-loaded.steps: A view loads the aurora photo. On its onLoad, getCachePath finds its file; then awaits FastImage.clearDiskCache(); then getCachePath with cache: 'cacheOnly', and then without it. Passes if the cacheOnly call resolves not ok, the other gives a file that's there, and the image server got two requests (the view's and the one after the clear).
cache-path-after-clear-loaded.shows: The aurora photo: the view, which keeps showing it after the clear.

description.checks: FastImage.clearDiskCache() doesn't hold up native calls made after it.

clear-disk-cache-thread.checks: clearDiskCache doesn't hold up a native call made after it (#1295: Android cleared the cache on React Native's native modules thread, so every module's async calls waited for it).
clear-disk-cache-thread.steps: Without awaiting, queues 200 getCachePath lookups with cache: 'cacheOnly' (images that aren't cached), then FastImage.clearDiskCache(), then getCachePath of a file:// uri, which is answered right away. Passes if the clear resolves ok and the file:// call resolves before it.
clear-disk-cache-thread.shows: An empty gray square: the case shows no image.

description.checks: FastImage.writeToCache: storing a local file as a source's image, and the cases where it resolves not ok.

write-to-cache.checks: writeToCache stores a local file as a url's image: a view of the url shows the file, without a request.
write-to-cache.steps: getCachePath downloads the aurora photo, and writeToCache stores its file as the image of a pug photo's url that nothing has loaded. Then a view shows that url. Passes on its onLoad if the image server got no request for the url.
write-to-cache.shows: The green aurora photo, not the pug the url would download.

write-to-cache-avif.checks: writeToCache with an AVIF file: a view of the url shows it, without a request (iOS rejected the file as not an image, since SDWebImage's format check didn't know AVIF; fixed in #1239).
write-to-cache-avif.steps: getCachePath downloads an AVIF of four colored quadrants, and writeToCache stores its file as the image of a pug photo's url. Then a view shows that url. Passes on its onLoad if the image server got no request for the url.
write-to-cache-avif.shows: Four quadrants: red, green, blue and yellow. The pug would mean the url was downloaded.

write-to-cache-key.checks: writeToCache for a source with a cacheKey: a view of that source shows the stored file, without a request.
write-to-cache-key.steps: getCachePath downloads the aurora photo, and writeToCache stores its file for a pug photo's url with a cacheKey. Then a view shows the same url and cacheKey. Passes on its onLoad if the image server got no request for the url.
write-to-cache-key.shows: The green aurora photo, not the pug.

write-to-cache-key-only.checks: writeToCache with only a cacheKey (no uri): a view of a url with that cacheKey shows the stored file, without a request.
write-to-cache-key-only.steps: getCachePath downloads the aurora photo, and writeToCache stores its file under only a cacheKey. Then a view shows a pug photo's url with that cacheKey. Passes on its onLoad if the image server got no request for the url.
write-to-cache-key-only.shows: The green aurora photo, not the pug.

write-to-cache-cached.checks: writeToCache for a url that's already cached doesn't replace its image: it resolves not ok.
write-to-cache-cached.steps: getCachePath downloads the aurora photo (the file) and the pug photo's url (so it's cached). Then writeToCache stores the file for the pug's url. Passes if it resolves not ok with 'Already in the disk cache'.
write-to-cache-cached.shows: An empty gray square: no view is shown.

write-to-cache-missing.checks: writeToCache with a file that doesn't exist resolves not ok.
write-to-cache-missing.steps: Calls writeToCache for a pug photo's url with file:///no/such/image.jpg. Passes if it resolves not ok with "Can't read the file".
write-to-cache-missing.shows: An empty gray square: no view is shown.

write-to-cache-web.checks: writeToCache for a cache: 'web' source resolves not ok: those images are kept by HTTP caching, not stored this way.
write-to-cache-web.steps: getCachePath downloads the aurora photo, and writeToCache stores its file for a pug photo's url with cache: 'web'. Passes if it resolves not ok with "Can't store cache: 'web'".
write-to-cache-web.shows: An empty gray square: no view is shown.

description.checks: Changing or clearing source while a slow image is still loading: the old load is cancelled, sends no events, and never replaces what is shown.

source-change-loading.checks: Changing source to a cached image while a slow image is still loading: no onError for the cancelled load, and the new image stays (#1159: iOS sent onError and onLoadEnd for the cancelled load).
source-change-loading.steps: Preloads a photo of a bear into the cache, then loads a cyan square from the slow server (in 8 parts, 150 ms apart: about 1.2 s). After 400 ms, changes source to the bear. Passes 1.5 s after its onLoad, once the slow load would have finished, if there was no onError and exactly one onLoad after the change.
source-change-loading.shows: The photo of a bear on rocks. A cyan square means the slow image replaced it.

source-change-keep-previous.checks: Changing source from a loaded image to a slow one, then to another image before the slow one loads: no onError for the cancelled load, and the last image stays (#1159: iOS sent onError and onLoadEnd for the cancelled load).
source-change-keep-previous.steps: Preloads a photo of a bear into the cache, then shows a magenta square. On its onLoad, changes source to a cyan square from the slow server (in 8 parts, 150 ms apart: about 1.2 s), which loads with the magenta one still showing. After 400 ms, changes source to the bear. Passes 1.5 s after its onLoad, once the slow load would have finished, if there was no onError and exactly one onLoad after the change.
source-change-keep-previous.shows: The photo of a bear on rocks. Magenta or cyan means a replaced image is showing.

source-change-data.checks: Changing source to a data uri while a slow image is still loading cancels the slow load: no onError or onLoad for it, and it doesn't replace the new image (#1159: iOS didn't cancel it for a data uri, so the slow image replaced the new one when it finished, with another onLoad).
source-change-data.steps: Loads a cyan square from the slow server (in 8 parts, 150 ms apart: about 1.2 s). After 400 ms, changes source to a data uri of an 8×8 yellow PNG. Passes 1.5 s after its onLoad, once the slow load would have finished, if there was no onError and exactly one onLoad after the change.
source-change-data.shows: A yellow square (the 8×8 image scaled up). A cyan square means the slow image replaced it.

source-cleared.checks: Clearing source while a slow image is still loading cancels the load: no onLoad, and the view stays blank (#1165: Android kept loading, then sent onLoad and showed the image).
source-cleared.steps: Loads a cyan square from the slow server (in 8 parts, 150 ms apart: about 1.2 s). After 400 ms, sets source to undefined. Passes 2 s after mount, once the load would have finished, if onLoad never fired.
source-cleared.shows: An empty gray square. A cyan square means the cancelled load finished and was shown.

description.checks: transition fades an image in when it loads: downloads and blurred images fade, images from the memory cache show at once unless skipOnCacheHit is none.
description.steps: Video samples: each case makes its change with the app's animations paused, then they're stepped through the fade with a screenshot at 0, 25, 50, 75 and 100% (where the app can't pause them, the screen is recorded). The color in the middle of its black 48 × 48 view must go through the listed colors in order. The runner turns fades off by default; these cases pass transition { duration: 1000 } (1 s), with the other settings each names.

fade.checks: transition fades a downloaded image in over its duration.
fade.steps: A black view mounts with a cyan image from the slow server (about 350 ms to download), with transition { duration: 1000 }. Recorded from the mount until 1.5 s after onLoad.
fade.shows: Recorded: black, then one steady fade through teal (half cyan) to cyan. At the end, a cyan square.

fade-memory.checks: With transition's default skipOnCacheHit ('memory'), an image from the memory cache shows at once, without a fade.
fade-memory.steps: A view (left) loads a cyan image; once it has, a second view (right, on black) mounts with the same source and transition { duration: 1000 }, so it comes from the memory cache. Recorded on the right until 1.5 s after its onLoad.
fade-memory.shows: Recorded: black, then cyan; never teal (half cyan, a fade). At the end, two cyan squares.

fade-memory-none.checks: transition with skipOnCacheHit: 'none' fades in an image from the memory cache too.
fade-memory-none.steps: A view (left) loads a cyan image; once it has, a second view (right, on black) mounts with the same source and transition { duration: 1000, skipOnCacheHit: 'none' }, so it comes from the memory cache.
fade-memory-none.shows: Recorded on the right: black, teal (half cyan), cyan. At the end, two cyan squares.

fade-blur.checks: transition with blurRadius: a downloaded image fades in already blurred.
fade-blur.steps: A black view mounts with a cyan image from the slow server (about 350 ms), with blurRadius={6} and transition { duration: 1000 }. Blurring a flat color keeps it, so the colors are those of a plain fade.
fade-blur.shows: Recorded: black, teal (half cyan), cyan. At the end, a cyan square.

description.checks: cache: 'web' images shown again: they show at once without transition and with it, and fade in with skipOnCacheHit none (Android faded them in each time, from its HTTP cache).
description.steps: Video samples, as in the fade group. In each case a view (left) loads a cyan image the server sends with Cache-Control: max-age=3600, with cache: 'web'; then a second view (right, on black) mounts with the same source: Android reads it from its HTTP cache without a request, iOS from the memory cache.

fade-web.checks: Without transition (the built-in default), a cache: 'web' image shown again from its HTTP cache shows at once (Android faded it in each time).
fade-web.steps: The right view has no transition prop, and the built-in default is turned back on for it (FastImage.setDefaults({ transition: null })), which fades on Android (300 ms) and not on iOS.
fade-web.shows: Recorded on the right: black, then cyan; never teal (half cyan, a fade). At the end, two cyan squares.

fade-web-transition.checks: transition: a cache: 'web' image shown again shows at once, on Android from its HTTP cache (Android faded it in each time).
fade-web-transition.steps: The right view has transition { duration: 1000 }.
fade-web-transition.shows: Recorded on the right: black, then cyan; never teal (half cyan, a fade). At the end, two cyan squares.

fade-web-none.checks: transition with skipOnCacheHit: 'none' fades in a cache: 'web' image shown again from its HTTP cache.
fade-web-none.steps: The right view has transition { duration: 1000, skipOnCacheHit: 'none' }.
fade-web-none.shows: Recorded on the right: black, teal (half cyan), cyan. At the end, two cyan squares.

description.checks: The built-in default transition: downloads fade in on Android (300 ms) and show at once on iOS.
description.steps: A video sample, as in the fade group.

fade-default.checks: Without transition, a downloaded image shows at once by default on iOS.
fade-default.steps: A black view mounts with a cyan image from the slow server (about 350 ms) and no transition prop, with the built-in default turned back on (FastImage.setDefaults({ transition: null }); the runner turns fades off otherwise).
fade-default.shows: Recorded: black, then cyan; never teal (half cyan, a fade). At the end, a cyan square.

description.checks: transition by where the image comes from: a new source from the memory cache shows at once, local files and bundled images fade in.
description.steps: Video samples, as in the fade group.

fade-change.checks: transition without betweenImages: a new source from the memory cache replaces the image showing at once, as in a reused list row.
fade-change.steps: A view (left) loads a cyan image; a second one (right, on black) shows a magenta image, with transition { duration: 1000 }. Once both have loaded (and 1.5 s more for the fades), the right view's source changes to the cyan one, from the memory cache.
fade-change.shows: Recorded on the right: magenta, then cyan; never blue-violet (a cross-dissolve). At the end, two cyan squares.

fade-file.checks: transition fades in a local file:// image: it isn't a memory cache hit.
fade-file.steps: A view (left) loads a cyan image; FastImage.getCachePath gives its file in the disk cache, and a second view (right, on black) mounts with that file as a file:// source and transition { duration: 1000 }.
fade-file.shows: Recorded on the right: black, teal (half cyan), cyan. At the end, two cyan squares.

fade-bundled.checks: transition fades in a bundled require() image too, not only downloaded ones.
fade-bundled.steps: A black view mounts with require('./images/cyan.png') (from Metro in debug builds, from the app in release builds) and transition { duration: 1000 }.
fade-bundled.shows: Recorded: black, teal (half cyan), cyan. At the end, a cyan square.

description.checks: transition's betweenImages: without it a new source replaces the image showing at once, with it the new image cross-dissolves from the old one.
description.steps: Video samples, as in the fade group. Each view shows a magenta image first, then its source changes to cyan.

fade-change-download.checks: transition without betweenImages: a new source that downloads replaces the image showing at once, once it has loaded.
fade-change-download.steps: The view (on black) shows a magenta image, with transition { duration: 1000 }; 1.5 s after it loads, its source changes to a cyan image from the slow server (about 350 ms).
fade-change-download.shows: Recorded: magenta (kept while cyan downloads), then cyan; never blue-violet (a cross-dissolve). At the end, a cyan square.

fade-between.checks: transition with betweenImages: a new source that downloads cross-dissolves from the image showing.
fade-between.steps: The view (on black) shows a magenta image, with transition { duration: 1000, betweenImages: true }; 1.5 s after it loads, its source changes to a cyan image from the slow server (about 350 ms).
fade-between.shows: Recorded: magenta, blue-violet (halfway), cyan. At the end, a cyan square.

fade-between-memory.checks: transition with betweenImages and skipOnCacheHit: 'none': a new source from the memory cache cross-dissolves from the image showing.
fade-between-memory.steps: A view (left) loads a cyan image; a second one (right, on black) shows a magenta image, with transition { duration: 1000, betweenImages: true, skipOnCacheHit: 'none' }. Once both have loaded (and 1.5 s more), the right view's source changes to the cyan one, from the memory cache.
fade-between-memory.shows: Recorded on the right: magenta, blue-violet (halfway), cyan. At the end, two cyan squares.

description.checks: transition from defaultSource: the image cross-dissolves from it, and defaultSource fades out under images with transparency and where the image doesn't cover the view (Android skips fading it out only under an opaque image that covers the view).

avif-loop-file.checks: Without loop, an animated AVIF that plays once by itself (no repetitions in the file) plays once and stops on its last frame.

avif-paused.checks: paused: an image (an animated AVIF) that loops forever by itself stays on its first frame.

avif-resume.checks: paused, then paused={false}, with loop={false} (an animated AVIF): the image plays once and stops on its last frame.

avif-resume.shows: A blue square (the last frame); red would mean resuming didn't play it.

webp-loop-remount.steps: Loads an animated WebP that loops forever (red, then blue) with loop={false}; after a play the view switches to another image (the quadrants), then a new view without loop shows the WebP again. blur-webp.checks: blurRadius on an animated WebP: it shows its first frame, blurred and still, as a blurred GIF does.
blur-webp.steps: Loads the animated WebP (red, then blue, 400 ms each, looping) with blurRadius 6. On onLoad it records the view for two plays. Passes when the recording sees only red.
blur-webp.shows: A red square (the first frame; blurring a flat color leaves it the same): masked, so not compared.

description.checks: SVG images (SDWebImageSVGCoder on iOS, AndroidSVG on Android, which Fast Image includes): remote and bundled, their sizes in onLoad, a wrong Content-Type, tintColor and downsample.

svg-remote.checks: A remote SVG loads, and onLoad has its own size.
svg-remote.steps: Loads the 100×50 SVG (left half red, right half blue) from the image server in a 96×48 view. Passes when onLoad has 100×50.
svg-remote.shows: A 96×48 rectangle: red on the left, blue on the right.

svg-bundled.checks: A require()d SVG, bundled with the app, loads, in debug and release builds.
svg-bundled.steps: Shows the 100×50 SVG (left half red, right half blue) from the app's bundle in a 96×48 view. Passes when onLoad has 100×50.
svg-bundled.shows: A 96×48 rectangle: red on the left, blue on the right.

svg-viewbox.checks: An SVG with only a viewBox (no width or height) loads, and onLoad has the viewBox's size.
svg-viewbox.steps: Loads an SVG with viewBox="0 0 60 30" (left half green, right half yellow) in a 64×32 view. Passes when onLoad has 60×30.
svg-viewbox.shows: A 64×32 rectangle: green on the left, yellow on the right.

svg-nosize.checks: An SVG with no width, height or viewBox loads at 300×150, the default size for one.
svg-nosize.steps: Loads an SVG without a size (a 300×150 magenta rectangle with a 150×150 cyan square on its left) in a 64×32 view. Passes when onLoad has 300×150.
svg-nosize.shows: A 64×32 rectangle: cyan on the left, magenta on the right (the whole SVG, scaled down).

svg-mislabeled.checks: An SVG the server sends with Content-Type: text/plain still loads.
svg-mislabeled.steps: Loads the 100×50 SVG (left half red, right half blue) from a server route that sends it as text/plain, in a 96×48 view. Passes when onLoad has 100×50.
svg-mislabeled.shows: A 96×48 rectangle: red on the left, blue on the right.

svg-tint.checks: tintColor on an SVG icon tints it.
svg-tint.steps: Loads a 24×24 SVG icon (a black ring) with tintColor green in a 48×48 view. Passes when onLoad has 24×24.
svg-tint.shows: A green ring filling the gray square; a black ring would mean the tint was ignored.

svg-downsample.checks: An SVG with downsample stays a vector image, drawn sharp, and onLoad has its own size (iOS drew it into a bitmap the view's size).
svg-downsample.steps: Loads the 100×50 SVG (left half red, right half blue) with downsample in a 96×48 view. Passes when onLoad has 100×50.
svg-downsample.shows: A 96×48 rectangle: red on the left, blue on the right, with a sharp edge between them.

description.checks: Images zoomed in on as a pinch-to-zoom viewer does, with downsample={false} and without, checked by screenshot.

zoom-transform.checks: A 30-point image scaled 4 times with a transform: downsample={false} keeps a photo sharp (decoded at full size), and an SVG as sharp as at its own size.
zoom-transform.steps: Four 30-point views in 120-point clips, each scaled 4 times about its center: a 1600x1000 page of text with downsample={false} and with downsample, then a 120x120 SVG of thin rings with downsample={false} and with downsample. Passes once all four have loaded; the screenshot checks the sharpness.
zoom-transform.shows: Top: large text, sharp on the left and blurry on the right. Bottom: thin rings filling the square, sharp on the left (iOS 10.9.8: soft, the SVG was drawn for 30 points) and soft on the right.

zoom-scroll-view.checks: A 30-point image in a ScrollView zoomed 4 times (zoomScale, iOS only), as a pinch-to-zoom viewer zooms: downsample={false} keeps a photo sharp, and an SVG as sharp as at its own size.
zoom-scroll-view.steps: Four 120-point ScrollViews with maximumZoomScale and zoomScale 4, each with a 30-point image: a 1600x1000 page of text with downsample={false} and with downsample, then a 120x120 SVG of thin rings with downsample={false} and with downsample. Passes once all four have loaded; the screenshot checks the sharpness.
zoom-scroll-view.shows: iOS: the same as zoom-transform. Android has no ScrollView zoom: four 30-point images in the top-left corners of their squares.

zoom-data-uri.checks: An SVG data uri with downsample={false}, scaled 4 times with a transform, is as sharp as at its own size, as from a url (iOS showed it as a vector, drawn for the view and scaled up).
zoom-data-uri.steps: A 30-point view in a 120-point clip, scaled 4 times about its center, shows a data uri of a 120x120 SVG of thin rings with downsample={false}. Passes once it has loaded; the screenshot checks the sharpness.
zoom-data-uri.shows: Thin rings filling the square, sharp (as zoom-transform's bottom left on iOS).

description.checks: How SVGs fit their views: objectFit contain and cover, and an SVG drawn sharp at a large size.

svg-contain.checks: objectFit="contain" on an SVG: the whole image fits inside the view.
svg-contain.steps: Loads the 100×50 SVG (left half red, right half blue) in a 64×64 view with objectFit="contain". Passes when onLoad has 100×50.
svg-contain.shows: A 64 pt square: a red and blue band across the middle (the whole SVG), with gray above and below.

svg-cover.checks: objectFit="cover" on an SVG: the image fills the view, cropped at the sides.
svg-cover.steps: Loads the 100×50 SVG (left half red, right half blue) in a 64×64 view with objectFit="cover". Passes when onLoad has 100×50.
svg-cover.shows: A 64 pt square, the left half red and the right half blue (the middle of the SVG); gray above and below would mean it was contained.

svg-sharp.checks: An SVG shown large is drawn at its size, not scaled up from a small bitmap.
svg-sharp.steps: Loads the same 20×20 SVG (three thin black rings on white) in a 24 pt view and a 160 pt view. Passes when both have fired onLoad; the sharpness is checked by the screenshot.
svg-sharp.shows: Small rings, then the same rings at 160 pt: thin, sharp black circles on white. Blurry or thick edges on the large one would mean it was scaled up from a bitmap.

svg-tint-placeholder.checks: A tinted SVG as the placeholder url, with objectFit none, is drawn for the size it fills, sharp (a url placeholder shows as with contain; drawn at its own size, 24 pt, it would be scaled up).
svg-tint-placeholder.steps: A 160 pt view with objectFit="none" and tintColor green loads a photo the slow server holds, with placeholder set to the url of a 24×24 SVG icon (a black ring). Passes 1 s after onLoadStart; onLoad fails it.
svg-tint-placeholder.shows: A green ring filling the 160 pt square, with sharp edges.

svg-full-size-larger.checks: An SVG with downsample={false} shown larger than its own size is drawn for the view, sharp, also when a smaller view of it loaded first (whose drawing the memory cache has).
svg-full-size-larger.steps: A 40 pt view loads a 20×20 SVG (three thin black rings on white) with downsample={false}; once it has loaded, a 160 pt view of the same url mounts. Passes a moment after that one loads; the screenshot checks the sharpness.
svg-full-size-larger.shows: The rings at 40 pt, then at 160 pt, both thin and sharp. Blurry or thick rings in the large one would mean it was scaled up from the small drawing.

description.checks: Photo library images (ph:// urls, iOS, with SDWebImagePhotosPlugin): a JPEG and a HEIC, a photo shown again after clearing the memory cache, an animated GIF, and urls that fail.
description.steps: Uses the simulator's photo library, which verify.mts grants access to and adds a GIF to (and on tvOS, whose simulator has no photos, a JPEG and a HEIC of the four colored quadrants).

photo-library-jpeg.checks: A JPEG from the photo library (a ph:// url) loads, and onLoad has the photo's own size, not the size it's decoded at (#410: local photos didn't load on iOS).
photo-library-jpeg.steps: Finds a JPEG in the simulator's photo library and shows it by its ph:// url in a 48 pt view. Passes when onLoad has the photo's width and height as the library lists them.
photo-library-jpeg.shows: A photo of a waterfall, cropped to fill the square (on tvOS, the four colored quadrants verify.mts adds).

photo-library-heic.checks: A HEIC photo from the photo library (a ph:// url) loads, and onLoad has the photo's own size, not the size it's decoded at (#410: local photos didn't load on iOS).
photo-library-heic.steps: Finds a HEIC photo in the simulator's photo library and shows it by its ph:// url in a 48 pt view. Passes when onLoad has the photo's width and height as the library lists them.
photo-library-heic.shows: A photo of pink and red flowers, cropped to fill the square (on tvOS, the four colored quadrants verify.mts adds).

photo-library-again.checks: A photo library photo shown again after FastImage.clearMemoryCache(), in a new view, still has its own size in onLoad, not the size it was decoded at (iOS reported the view-sized copy, which it had stored on disk as the photo).
photo-library-again.steps: Finds a JPEG in the simulator's photo library and shows it (ph://) in a 48 pt view. On onLoad it checks the size, calls clearMemoryCache and shows the photo in a new view. Passes when the second onLoad also has the photo's own size.
photo-library-again.shows: The same photo as the JPEG row (a waterfall; the four colored quadrants on tvOS), cropped to fill the square.

photo-library-gif.checks: A GIF from the photo library (ph://) animates.
photo-library-gif.steps: Finds the GIF verify.mts adds to the simulator's library (red, then blue, 400 ms each, looping) and shows it with paused and loop={false}. On onLoad it starts recording and sets paused={false}, so it plays once.
photo-library-gif.shows: A blue square (the last frame). Recorded: red, then blue.

photo-library-missing.checks: A ph:// url whose id isn't in the photo library fails with onError.
photo-library-missing.steps: Loads ph://00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000/L0/001, an id no photo has. Passes when onError's error mentions the localIdentifier.
photo-library-missing.shows: An empty gray square: nothing loads.

photo-library-assets-library.checks: An assets-library:// url (the old camera roll url) fails with onError, with a message pointing to ph:// urls (#314: they showed a blank image on iOS, with no error).
photo-library-assets-library.steps: Loads an assets-library://asset/asset.JPG?id=… url. Passes when onError's error mentions ph://.
photo-library-assets-library.shows: An empty gray square: nothing loads.

description.checks: FastImage.configureCache and the disk cache limit set in the native config.

configure-cache.checks: FastImage.configureCache: the maxDiskSize in the app's native config (300 MB) is in effect from the start, with the disk cache's size; a runtime change applies (iOS at once, Android from the next launch), and null resets it.
configure-cache.steps: Reads configureCache(): the limit, and a disk size above 0 from earlier groups' images. iOS: downloads a photo with getCachePath, sets maxDiskSize to 1 byte, which empties the disk cache, checks the photo is gone (getCachePath with cache: 'cacheOnly'), then resets it with null. Android: sets 1 byte, then null, and the limit in effect stays 300 MB. Passes when every value matches.
configure-cache.shows: An empty gray square: no image is shown.

description.checks: preload, getCachePath and writeToCache with a url string where a source object goes: each resolves not ok instead of crashing the app.

preload-non-object.checks: FastImage.preload with a url string or a number where a source object goes resolves that entry not ok, in its place among the results (#592: native read it as a source and crashed the app: Android cast it to a map, iOS sent it an unrecognized selector).
preload-non-object.steps: Preloads a url string, then { uri } with the same 200×200 photo, then the number 42. Passes when the results are, in order: not ok ('Invalid source: no uri'), ok at 200x200, not ok.
preload-non-object.shows: An empty gray square: no image is shown.

cache-path-non-object.checks: FastImage.getCachePath with a url string where a source object goes resolves not ok with an error (native read it as a source and crashed the app).
cache-path-non-object.steps: Calls FastImage.getCachePath with a url string as the source. Passes when it resolves { ok: false } with an error.
cache-path-non-object.shows: An empty gray square: no image is shown.

write-to-cache-non-object.checks: FastImage.writeToCache with a url string where a source object goes resolves not ok with an error (native read it as a source and crashed the app).
write-to-cache-non-object.steps: Calls FastImage.writeToCache with a url string as the source and a file path that doesn't exist. Passes when it resolves { ok: false } with an error.
write-to-cache-non-object.shows: An empty gray square: no image is shown.
